v04.text: Boston. In August 1900, 4 Harvard students challenged Britain to a tennis match at the Longwood Cricket Club.

v05.text: The British team crossed the Atlantic by steamship, and lost all 3 matches on grass.

v06.text: Dwight Davis paid for the silver trophy out of his own pocket, and the cup still carries his name.

v07.text: The United States has won it 32 times, Australia 28. Nobody else has reached 11.

v08.text: A student dare that never stopped. Follow us.

research.topic: First Davis Cup (International Lawn Tennis Challenge), 8–10 August 1900, Longwood Cricket Club, Boston: United States beat the British Isles 3–0; conceived by 4 Harvard players; Dwight F. Davis bought the sterling trophy; all-time titles USA 32, Australia 28, GB 10, France 10.

myths.myth: The Davis Cup began in England, the home of lawn tennis.
myths.reality: It began in Boston as an American challenge to the British; Britain won its first Cup only in 1903.
